The source further explains that this combination addresses the issue of overfitting (or performance decline in high-frequency regions) and preserves fine structural details (high-frequency details). All specific components and goals mentioned in the claim are present in the evidence.

SGCNeRF is a few-shot neural rendering architecture for novel view synthesis that addresses the performance decline of standard frequency regularization in high-frequency regions (rich textures or geometry variations) where methods like FreeNeRF suffer from excessive smoothing [S1].

The claim is fully supported by the evidence in Source [S1]. The source explicitly identifies SGCNeRF as a 'few-shot neural rendering architecture' for 'novel view synthesis'. It states that standard frequency regularization (used by methods like FreeNeRF) suffers from 'excessive smoothing' and a 'notable decline in performance' in 'high-frequency regions' (rich textures/geometry variations). The source further confirms that SGCNeRF addresses this specific issue by using 'sparse geometric consistency guidance' (via sparse feature matching and geometric optimization) to preserve high-frequency details where FreeNeRF struggles.
